title: Menelik II
summary: Menelik II (1844–1913) became Emperor of Ethiopia in 1889 after the death of Yohannes IV. He founded Addis Ababa as his capital in 1886 while still King of Shewa, and in 1896 defeated an Italian invasion at the Battle of Adwa, securing Ethiopia's independence during the European partition of Africa. His reign expanded the empire southward and began modern state institutions.

uncertainty.note: Life dates 1844–1913 per Ethiopia: A Political History (days not given on opened pages); coronation 3 November 1889 per Library of Congress; Addis Ababa 1886 per World History Edu; Adwa 1 March 1896 per Ethiopia: A Political History.

importance.justification: Emperor who preserved Ethiopian independence at Adwa and founded the modern capital Addis Ababa.
